consent.title: Talk with Céoù
consent.body: To hold a real conversation, your voice is streamed live to Gemini, Google’s artificial intelligence service, outside the European Union. As the conversation goes, Céoù also passes it the results of your searches — item names and where they are stored — but never your whole inventory. Nothing is sent until the conversation is open. When it is unavailable, the simple assistant takes over: only the text of your sentence is sent then.

demarrer.title: Getting started
demarrer.summary: Understand how Céoù stores things, and put your first item away.
demarrer.goal: Put your first belonging away, and know how to find it by typing its name.
steps: Create your home. A house, a flat — but also a garage, a cellar or a vehicle.
Add a room: the kitchen, your bedroom. A garage or a cellar has none, you store things directly there.
Add a storage unit in that room: a dresser, a shelf, a cupboard, a desk.
If your things are in a box, add the box. Otherwise skip this step: it is not required.
Put your item inside, with its photo. Then search for it from the home screen.
demarrer.tip: Do not store everything at once. Start with what you look for most often: papers, tools, cables, chargers.
demarrer.result: You type “scissors” on the home screen, and Céoù answers with the full path. You can also ask out loud.
demarrer.action_hint: Two minutes, and it creates everything with you.

factures.title: Your receipts and warranties
factures.summary: Keep proof of what you own, and send it as a single file.
factures.goal: Attach proof of purchase to your items, get warned before a warranty ends, and be able to send it all to your insurer.
steps: Open an item page and tap “Add a receipt”.
Photograph the till receipt — or import the PDF the shop emailed you.
Note the seller, the purchase date, the amount, and the warranty end date if the item has one.
One receipt can cover several items. Open it from the home’s Receipts screen and add them: each keeps its own amount and warranty.
From another item page, choose “One already saved” to attach it to the same receipt without photographing the paper again.
The “Without receipt” tab lists everything with no proof yet. The export button, at the top, builds the complete file.
factures.tip: Fill in the warranty end date even when it feels far off. Céoù warns you thirty days before — the only moment it can still be of use.
factures.result: A single PDF: the itemised summary of your purchases, then every supporting document. Ready to email your insurer.

retrouver.title: Finding a belonging
retrouver.summary: By searching, or by asking out loud.
retrouver.goal: Ask “where is…” and get the exact path, hands full or not.
steps: On the home screen, type the start of the name. The list narrows with every letter.
Each result shows its full path: the home, the room, the furniture, the box.
With your hands full, tap the mic instead and ask: “where are my scissors?”. Céoù answers out loud.
You can also put things away by voice: “put the drill on the workbench”. Céoù does it, and offers to undo if you misspoke.
When it hesitates between two items or two places, it asks you rather than choosing on its own.
retrouver.tip: Céoù never invents a place. If it cannot find the furniture you name, it says so and stores nothing — a refusal beats an item dropped anywhere.
retrouver.result: You know where a belonging is in three seconds, without opening a single screen.

ajouter-vite.title: Adding many items
ajouter-vite.summary: Scan a photo or a barcode instead of typing everything.
ajouter-vite.goal: Fill a whole shelf without writing thirty names by hand.
steps: From a storage unit, choose “Scan a photo”.
Photograph the shelf or the open drawer, framing it wide.
Céoù offers one line per item recognised. Untick what is not an item, fix the names, and confirm in one go.
For a shop-bought product there is a shortcut: “Scan a barcode” fills in the name and the photo on its own.
If the code is unknown it is still kept: you fill in the rest by hand.
ajouter-vite.tip: Detection goes through an outside service, and Céoù asks for your consent the first time. The barcode only queries a public product directory.
ajouter-vite.result: A shelf of fifteen items enters the inventory in one photo and two corrections.

plan.title: Your home’s floor plan
plan.summary: Draw your rooms, and see where your belongings sit.
plan.goal: Move from words to a drawing: show where something is instead of describing it.
steps: From a home, open “Plan”. Starting from nothing, pick a typical layout — studio, two rooms, house — and everything is drawn for you.
In “Edit” mode, tap a room to select it, drag it to move it, pull the blue dots to resize it.
“Door” then a tap on a wall opens it up; keep your finger down and slide to move it along the wall.
The pins are your storage units. A tap picks one, a drag places it in the room, a double-tap removes it from the plan.
In “Explore” mode, tapping a room tells you what it holds — and from an item page, “View on plan” takes you straight there.
plan.tip: The “View as list” button tells the same plan in words — “top left”, “centre”. It is quicker to scan than a drawing, and it stays readable when eyesight is not.
plan.result: You open the plan, tap the kitchen, and see the four storage units it holds.

prets.title: Lending and borrowing
prets.summary: Remember what left your home, and what you owe back.
prets.goal: Stop hunting for who has your drill, or forgetting the book you were lent.
steps: On an item page, tap “Lend or borrow”.
Say which way it goes: you are lending it, or you borrowed it.
Pick a friend from the list, or simply type a name — the person does not need to have Céoù.
Set a return date if you have one: Céoù will remind you on the day. Without a date, the loan stays in the list until you close it.
When the item comes back, a button on its page or in the Loans screen closes the loan.
prets.tip: A lent item does not leave your inventory: it keeps its place, which is where it will return. A banner on its page only reminds you that it is not there right now.
prets.result: The Loans screen lists what is out, overdue first.

amis.title: Sharing with people close to you
amis.summary: Give access to a home, and choose how far it goes.
amis.goal: Let someone else see — or edit — the inventory of a home you share.
steps: In Profile, show your friend code: eight characters, or its QR. It never changes.
They enter it in “Add a friend”, or scan the QR. A request reaches you.
Until you share something, they see nothing: accepting someone grants access to no home at all.
Open their page, and choose for each home: no access, read-only, edit, or owner.
Sort your friends into categories — family, flatmates, neighbours — once the list grows.
amis.tip: The permission is set per HOME, not per person. Your partner can edit the house and see nothing of the garage.
amis.result: They see your home on their own home screen, with exactly the rights you gave them.

invites.title: Access with no account
invites.summary: A read-only code for a tenant, a tradesperson, a house-sitter.
invites.goal: Show a home to someone who does not have Céoù, and does not want to install it.
steps: In Profile, choose “Generate an access code”.
Tick the homes concerned. A guest only gets read-only access: they can change or add nothing.
Set the duration and the number of uses — or make the code permanent, for someone who stays.
Give it a name, “July tenants” for instance: that is what will let you recognise it later.
Share the link or the code. They enter it in “I have an invitation code”, with no account to create.
invites.tip: Your codes live in “My invitation codes”. Deleting one cuts access immediately, including for people already using it.
invites.result: Your tenant browses the home’s inventory from their phone, with no account and nothing they can change.

affichage.title: Adjusting the display
affichage.goal: Fit Céoù to your eyes and your light, not the other way round.
steps: In Profile, open “Display”.
Choose the text size: normal, large, very large. It is not only the text — buttons, images and spacing grow with it.
A preview shows the result before you leave the screen.
Dark mode follows your phone by default. You can force it either way.
The language changes in the same place, and applies straight away.
affichage.tip: If your phone is already set to enlarged text, Céoù follows it with nothing for you to do — and says so in the Display screen.
affichage.result: The whole app resizes: lists, pages, the plan, the tutorials.

hors-ligne.title: With no network
hors-ligne.summary: What Céoù can do in a cellar or a garage.
hors-ligne.goal: Store, photograph and search where there is no signal — that is, where you actually store things.
steps: A banner appears at the top when the connection drops. You see the last data loaded.
You can still create, rename, move, photograph: everything is written on the phone and shows up immediately.
Céoù queues those changes and sends them on its own when the network returns.
Search works too: your inventory is loaded in advance, including pages you have never opened.
If the server refuses a change, it is not lost: a banner flags it and you can retry or drop it.
hors-ligne.tip: Only two things need the network: exporting your receipts, which has to download the documents again, and speech recognition.
hors-ligne.result: You store your cellar with no signal, and everything goes up when you come back out.
